members.label: CS-80
members.differences: The original, Yamaha's 1977 polysynth: eight voices of two layered voices per note, a ribbon controller, and a keyboard that responds to velocity and to pressure on each key. Heard on Vangelis’s Blade Runner score.

members.label: DS-80 (announced)
members.differences: Announced, not yet on sale. Behringer's planned copy of the CS-80, first mentioned in July 2020. A prototype board shown in April 2022 held two voices and the digital control section, and nothing more had been said by January 2025.

members.label: Deckard’s Dream
members.differences: Black Corporation’s analogue module built on the CS-80’s voice, which its maker calls a revival rather than a clone: the same two layers per note, IL-AL-A-D-R filter envelope and sine past the filters, with no keyboard, ribbon, ring modulator, chorus or preset rows. Its P/G switch has a centre where nothing glides. It is played over MIDI with polyphonic aftertouch and MPE and stores presets, and the MK2 adds a master SUSTAIN slider and puts sample and hold where the MK1 had an external input.
